text:
jane-security: quick one — we need a concise process for customer-facing audit exports + cryptographic proof of immutability for retained logs. Scope: schema we publish, how manifests/signatures work, what storage configuration (WORM/Object Lock), and RBAC for export requests. Any major missing pieces?

mike-ops: +1. also: legal-hold flow. customers might ask for an export while a hold is active — do we block or provide a sealed export with hold flag?

alyssa: sketching a minimal event schema we can publish to customers (suggestions welcome):
```json
{
  "event_id": "uuid4",
  "timestamp": "iso8601",
  "actor": "user_id|service",
  "action": "string",
  "resource": "arn-like",
  "request_id": "trace-id",
  "before": "optional-json",
  "after": "optional-json",
  "trace": "span-ids[]",
  "signature": "base64(sig)",
  "prev_hash": "hex(sha256)"
}
```
We add signature+prev_hash to support append-only hash chains and allow offline verification.

kevin-engineering: prefer separating the signing key from the encryption key. Use an asymmetric signing key (ECDSA/secp384r1) stored in KMS or HSM and only expose Sign/GetPublicKey APIs. Encryption of objects can still use a separate CMK. Note: KMS Sign API has limits, we may need a short-lived signer service for high throughput.

sam-legal: retention rules: default 7y for audit-relevant actions, exceptions for regulatory customers (varies). Legal hold must prevent deletion and should be surfaced in the export metadata. If we provide an export during hold, include a signed manifest that marks it as "subject_to_hold": true and list hold id + cust contact.

devops_bot: backup-job: full-audit-dump-2026-03-10 finished, manifest uploaded to s3://redwood-audit-archive/2026/03/10/manifest.json (sealed) :white_check_mark:

jane-security: proposed export playbook (high level):
- customer requests export via Console/API -> exports queue
- verify RBAC: only accounts with role:audit_exporter + 2FA/sys-approval can enqueue
- security review auto-if flagged (sensitive PII) -> manual approval if needed
- create a sealed package: events.json.gz + manifest.json + signatures
- store package in WORM bucket (Object Lock Governance/Compliance) with retention TTL = max(customer retention, legal_hold)
- deliver signed reference (S3 URL + manifest signature + public key id) to customer

mike-ops: RBAC detail: add new IAM role "audit_exporter" scoped to the export API + console action. Require a security approver to be in the approval chain for orgs with >100 seats. Also require request justification in the API call.

alyssa: storage config notes: create buckets with Object Lock enabled at creation time and enable S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode for final manifests. Example: create bucket + enable default retention (aws cli):
```bash
aws s3api create-bucket --bucket redwood-audit-archive --object-lock-enabled-for-bucket --region us-east-1
aws s3api put-object-retention --bucket redwood-audit-archive --key "2026/03/10/manifest.json" --retention "{\"Mode\":\"COMPLIANCE\",\"RetainUntilDate\":\"2033-03-10T00:00:00Z\"}"
```
Note: Object Lock must be set when creating the bucket. Also enable default encryption using CMK: kms:Encrypt and kms:Sign need distinct key policies.

kevin-engineering: vulnerability triage question — if signing key is suspected compromised, how do we prove prior manifests are still valid? options:
- maintain an append-only root key history signed by an offline HSM (timestamped certs)
- publish periodic checkpoint hashes (e.g., daily root hash) signed by an offline root key and cross-signed by KMS key
Re-issuing signatures for old manifests is unacceptable. We need a rotation scheme that preserves verifiability.

sam-legal: that matches legal requirements — we need non-repudiation. please document the checkpoint cadence (daily) and retention of signed checkpoints for the statutory period.

jane-security: action items / owners: 
- alyssa: draft "audit export schema" doc + sample verifier CLI (due: 2 business days)
- kevin-engineering: design key rotation+checkpoint proposal with threat scenarios (due: 5 business days)
- mike-ops: PR for IAM role "audit_exporter" + console flow + API param for justification (due: 3 business days)
- sam-legal: provide exact retention ranges by regulation (due: 4 business days)

alyssa: one nuance — customers may want to verify without pulling the whole archive. propose we publish a manifest index with byte-range offsets + per-chunk SHA256 so they can fetch pieces and verify. will add to doc.

mike-ops: small operational note: ensure export generation job never runs on overloaded inference nodes. route to dedicated export worker pool.

jane-security: thanks all. I'll raise a short RFC for sign/manifest format and link to this thread. tagging for awareness: @here if you want to weigh in on the schema/retention choices. :lock:
